main_point.en: Jesus forgives us when we humbly come to Him in faith.
main_point.zh-Hant: 當我們憑信心謙卑地來到耶穌面前，祂就赦免我們。

christ_connection.en: Our sin created debt, a payment so extreme that we could never repay it with our own good works or sacrifice. Instead, Jesus willingly surrendered Himself as the sacrifice for our sin. He paid our debt with His blood and covered us permanently.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 我們的罪造成了債務，代價大得我們永遠無法靠自己的善行或犧牲償還。耶穌卻甘願捨己，為我們的罪獻上自己為祭。祂用自己的血償清我們的債，永遠遮蓋我們的罪。

title.en: Jesus Is Willing to Forgive Us

content.en:
36 One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, and he went into the Pharisee’s house and reclined at table. 
37 And behold, a woman of the city, who was a sinner, when she learned that he was reclining at table in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster flask of ointment, 
38 and standing behind him at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment. 
39 Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him, for she is a sinner.”
content.zh-Hant:
36 有一個法利賽人請耶穌和他吃飯；耶穌就到法利賽人家裏去坐席。
37 那城裏有一個女人，是個罪人，知道耶穌在法利賽人家裏坐席，就拿著盛香膏的玉瓶，
38 站在耶穌背後，挨著他的腳哭，眼淚濕了耶穌的腳，就用自己的頭髮擦乾，又用嘴連連親他的腳，把香膏抹上。
39 請耶穌的法利賽人看見這事，心裏說：「這人若是先知，必知道摸他的是誰，是個怎樣的女人；乃是個罪人。」

content.en:
40 And Jesus answering said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he answered, “Say it, Teacher.” 
41 “A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. 
42 When they could not pay, he cancelled the debt of both. Now which of them will love him more?” 
43 Simon answered, “The one, I suppose, for whom he cancelled the larger debt.” And he said to him, “You have judged rightly.” 
44 Then turning toward the woman he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. 
45 You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not ceased to kiss my feet. 
46 You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment. 
47 Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little.” 
48 And he said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.” 
49 Then those who were at table with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this, who even forgives sins?” 
50 And he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
content.zh-Hant:
40 耶穌對他說：「西門！我有句話要對你說。」西門說：「夫子，請說。」
41 耶穌說：「一個債主有兩個人欠他的債；一個欠五十兩銀子，一個欠五兩銀子；
42 因為他們無力償還，債主就開恩免了他們兩個人的債。這兩個人哪一個更愛他呢？」
43 西門回答說：「我想是那多得恩免的人。」耶穌說：「你斷的不錯。」
44 於是轉過來向著那女人，便對西門說：「你看見這女人嗎？我進了你的家，你沒有給我水洗腳；但這女人用眼淚濕了我的腳，用頭髮擦乾。
45 你沒有與我親嘴；但這女人從我進來的時候就不住地用嘴親我的腳。
46 你沒有用油抹我的頭；但這女人用香膏抹我的腳。
47 所以我告訴你，她許多的罪都赦免了，因為她的愛多；但那赦免少的，他的愛就少。」
48 於是對那女人說：「你的罪赦免了。」
49 同席的人心裏說：「這是甚麼人，竟赦免人的罪呢？」
50 耶穌對那女人說：「你的信救了你；平平安安回去吧！」

content.en: Leaders: Consider when you've been like the woman, spilling out your sin and receiving forgiveness; consider when you’ve been the Pharisee, comparing your sin to someone else’s.
content.zh-Hant: 領袖：想想自己何時像那位婦人，傾吐自己的罪並領受赦免；也想想自己何時像法利賽人，將自己的罪與別人的罪相比。

title.en: Jesus Is Willing to Forgive Us

content.en: “In Jewish society at that time, it was scandalous and indecent for a woman to let down her hair in public. It seems probable that she was a prostitute or perhaps an adulteress (7:37), so perhaps she was callous to the cultural norm, but it is more likely she was overcome with repentance and thankfulness (2 Sam. 6:16-23). Accordingly, Jesus passed over the scandal and emphasized to her and to those around Him the forgiveness and salvation available to all who repent and believe (7:48, 50). Christian women were later instructed to dress modestly and decently (1 Tim. 2:9).”⁸
content.zh-Hant: 「在當時的猶太社會，婦人在公眾面前披散頭髮是令人震驚、不體面的。她很可能是妓女或淫婦（7:37），因此或許對文化規範不以為意，但更可能的是，她因悔改和感恩而情難自禁（撒母耳記下 6:16-23）。因此，耶穌沒有在意這件令人側目的事，反而向她和周圍的人強調，凡悔改並相信的人都可以得到赦免和救恩（7:48、50）。後來，基督徒婦女受教導要穿著端莊、得體（提摩太前書 2:9）。」⁸

content.en: “With relationship to others, man is a fellow-debtor whose pretensions of moral and religious superiority are completely irrelevant. . . . All are hopelessly in debt, but some delude themselves into believing that theirs is not so great by comparison with others. The parable also teaches that God is not like men, harshly demanding his pound of flesh. He freely forgives men their debts.”⁹
content.zh-Hant: 「在人與人的關係中，每個人都是同欠債的人，自以為在道德和宗教上優越的主張毫無意義。……所有人都欠下無望償還的債，但有些人自欺，以為自己的債比別人的少。這個比喻也教導我們，神不像人那樣嚴苛地要求償債。祂白白赦免人的債。」⁹

content.en: “It would have been expected that the host would have provided water for his guest’s feet (Gen. 18:4; Judg. 19:21). Jesus had not received this courtesy, but He had had His feet washed with the woman’s tears. Similarly, in place of the kiss of welcome that might have been expected from the host (Gen. 29:13; 45:15) He had received kisses on His feet. And finally, whereas Simon had omitted to anoint Jesus’s head (Pss. 23:5; 141:5), the woman had anointed His feet (oil is olive oil, which was plentiful and cheap; there is a contrast with ointment, which was rare and expensive perfume).”¹⁰
content.zh-Hant: 「人們會期望主人給客人水洗腳（創世記 18:4；士師記 19:21）。耶穌沒有受到這樣的禮待，卻讓那婦人用眼淚洗了腳。同樣，主人或許應當以親嘴迎接祂（創世記 29:13；45:15），祂卻得到了婦人對祂腳的親吻。最後，西門沒有用油抹耶穌的頭（詩篇 23:5；141:5），那婦人卻用香膏抹祂的腳（油指的是充足而便宜的橄欖油，與稀有昂貴的香膏形成對比）。」¹⁰

content.en: When we invite people over, we follow certain steps to prepare our home so guests are comfortable while they’re visiting. We call this hospitality. People in Jesus’s day showed hospitality by offering specific things when guests entered their homes too. For example, people wore sandals and traveled mostly by foot on dirt roads, so hosts usually offered guests water to wash their feet. Failure to do so would’ve been considered an insult—which is exactly what happened when Jesus entered the home of Simon the Pharisee. But that wasn’t the only common courtesy Simon ignored: He didn’t greet Jesus with a kiss (elsewhere called a “holy kiss”; an affectionate but not inappropriate or romantic greeting that shows respect), and he failed to anoint Jesus’s head with oil (to show honor). However, the woman, only described here as a “sinner,” did all these things for Jesus: She washed Jesus’s feet with her tears and wiped them clean with her hair, and she kissed His feet and anointed them with expensive perfume. Scripture doesn’t tell us Simon’s motive for inviting Jesus into his home, but his lack of hospitality tells us he probably didn’t hold a high opinion of Jesus. Though Simon believed he was a prime example of righteousness, this woman proved him wrong. She humbled herself before the One who deserves our honest worship, and He forgave her sin.
content.zh-Hant: 當我們邀請人到家裏來，會做一些準備，好讓客人來訪時感到舒適。我們稱這為款待。耶穌時代的人也會在客人進門時提供特定的款待。例如，人們穿涼鞋，大多走在塵土路上，所以主人通常會給客人水洗腳。不這樣做會被視為一種侮辱，而耶穌進入法利賽人西門家中時，正是如此。但西門忽略的常規禮節不只這一項：他沒有以親嘴迎接耶穌（別處稱為「聖潔的親嘴」；這是親切、表達尊重的問候，並非不恰當或浪漫的舉動），也沒有用油抹耶穌的頭以示尊敬。然而，這裏只被稱為「罪人」的婦人，卻為耶穌做了這一切：她用眼淚洗耶穌的腳，用頭髮擦乾，並親吻祂的腳，用昂貴的香膏抹祂的腳。聖經沒有告訴我們西門邀請耶穌到家的動機，但他缺乏款待表明，他可能並不看重耶穌。西門雖然認為自己是義人的典範，這婦人卻證明他錯了。她在那位配得我們真誠敬拜的主面前謙卑自己，祂就赦免了她的罪。

content.en: Biblical faith is the resting, or trusting, in Christ alone for salvation (John 3:16-21). More than being simply a mental agreement of historical facts, genuine faith begins with a recognition and confession of the truth of the gospel (1 John 4:13-16), followed by a receiving of Christ as Lord and Savior of one’s life (John 1:10-13). Biblical faith is not blind faith, for it rests on the historical life, death, and resurrection of Christ.
content.zh-Hant: 聖經所說的信心，是單單信靠基督得救（約翰福音 3:16-21）。真正的信心不只是頭腦上認同歷史事實，而是從認識並承認福音的真理開始（約翰一書 4:13-16），然後接受基督為自己生命的主和救主（約翰福音 1:10-13）。聖經所說的信心不是盲目的，因為它以基督在歷史中的生、死和復活為根據。

content.en: LORD JESUS, YOU ARE OUR PERFECT SAVIOR. THANK YOU FOR HUMBLING YOURSELF TO DIE ON THE CROSS FOR US. MAY WE HUMBLE OURSELVES BEFORE YOU IN WORSHIP AND TEACH OUR STUDENTS TO DO THE SAME.
content.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，祢是我們完美的救主。感謝祢謙卑自己，為我們死在十字架上。願我們在敬拜中於祢面前謙卑自己，也教導學生這樣做。

content.en: Let’s check in on how you’re doing spiritually. Last week, we talked about some heavy things. How has the truth that Jesus has power over life and death helped you feel more hopeful about death, loss, and grief? What opportunities have you had to walk with others and point them to hope?
content.zh-Hant: 讓我們看看你目前的屬靈狀況。上週我們談了一些沉重的事。耶穌掌管生死這個真理，如何幫助你面對死亡、失落和悲傷時更有盼望？你有甚麼機會與別人同行，帶領他們看見盼望？

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You'll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些自選活動旨在幫助學生互動。當中包括討論活動和文化連結，後者觸及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不同，請按小組需要調整活動。目的是讓學生在接觸主題和彼此交流時，更投入課程。

提出以下問題，留時間讓學生分享答案：

question.en: WHAT'S THE MOST UNUSUAL THING SOMEONE HAS THANKED YOU FOR?
question.zh-Hant: 別人曾為甚麼最不尋常的事情感謝你？

question.en: HOW WOULD YOU EXPRESS YOUR GRATITUDE TO SOMEONE WHO HAS DONE SOMETHING HUGE FOR YOU?
question.zh-Hant: 如果有人為你做了一件非常重大的事，你會如何向他表達感謝？

question.en: WHEN DO YOU STRUGGLE TO SHOW GRATITUDE? WHY?
question.zh-Hant: 你甚麼時候難以表達感謝？為甚麼？

content.en: Showing gratitude isn’t always easy—whether an unexpected gift leaves us shocked or speechless or our thanks feels forced because the gift didn’t live up to our expectations or come from the right person. But Jesus deserves all our gratitude and worship. Despite our sin against Him, He willingly died to offer us forgiveness, salvation, and a restored relationship with God forever. Today, we’ll see what it means to humble ourselves and be forgiven.
content.zh-Hant: 表達感謝並不總是容易：意外的禮物可能讓我們驚訝得說不出話來；禮物若不合期望或來自不合心意的人，我們的感謝也可能顯得勉強。但耶穌配得我們一切的感謝和敬拜。儘管我們得罪了祂，祂仍甘願受死，賜給我們赦免、救恩和與神永遠恢復的關係。今天我們要看看謙卑自己並蒙赦免是甚麼意思。

cultural_connection.en: When people hurt us—even people we don’t know—letting go of the hurt isn’t easy. We might vent to our friends or even share a post on social media. Our temptation is to hold nothing back, to give up every detail. Maybe our goal is to shame the other person or to justify our feelings or responses; maybe we’re just looking for sympathy on a bad day. Over time, maybe we cool down and offer forgiveness. Or, maybe we double down, and bitterness grows into a grudge. But here’s the whole, tough truth: We have no right to hold grudges or withhold forgiveness. If anyone had a right to hold a grudge, Jesus did. But He did the opposite; He withheld nothing from us, giving His very life to bring life to us when we were dead in our sin (Eph. 2:1). Certainly, we might need to set boundaries for physical and emotional safety, but forgiveness can exist within those boundaries. Forgiveness heals our hearts and sets us free; unforgiveness holds us captive. Just as Jesus forgave us and set us free, so we must be willing to forgive others.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 當人傷害我們，即使是我們不認識的人，要放下傷痛也不容易。我們可能向朋友發洩，甚至在社交媒體上發文。我們很容易忍不住毫無保留地說出每個細節。也許我們想讓對方蒙羞，或證明自己的感受或回應有理；也許只是在糟糕的一天尋求同情。過了一段時間，我們可能冷靜下來，願意饒恕；也可能更加執著，讓苦毒長成怨恨。但完整而難以接受的事實是：我們沒有權利懷恨或拒絕饒恕。若有人有權懷恨，那就是耶穌。但祂做的恰恰相反：祂毫無保留地捨去自己的生命，在我們死在罪中時賜給我們生命（以弗所書 2:1）。當然，為了身心安全，我們可能需要設立界限，但饒恕可以在這些界限內存在。饒恕醫治我們的心，使我們自由；不饒恕則使我們受捆綁。正如耶穌赦免我們、釋放我們，我們也必須願意饒恕別人。

title.en: Jesus Is Willing To Forgive Us

question.en: Describe the woman in the passage. What do her actions reveal about her heart?
question.zh-Hant: 描述經文中的婦人。她的行動顯示她有怎樣的心？

answer.en: Labeled a sinner, this woman demonstrated great courage by visiting Jesus in the home of a Pharisee. She approached Jesus humbly, recognizing her sin, His holiness, and her desperate need for forgiveness. With tears, she mourned over her sin and held on to the hope Jesus offered. She didn’t put on a show for others; she showed love and commitment to the One who would save her from her sin. May we recognize our brokenness and sin, and may we also kneel at Jesus’s feet with humility and hope, admitting our desperate need to be forgiven.
answer.zh-Hant: 這婦人被視為罪人，卻鼓起極大的勇氣到法利賽人家中見耶穌。她謙卑地來到耶穌面前，認識到自己的罪、祂的聖潔，以及自己迫切需要赦免。她流淚為自己的罪哀傷，緊緊抓住耶穌所賜的盼望。她不是做給別人看，而是向那位要把她從罪中拯救出來的主表達愛和委身。願我們認清自己的破碎和罪，也帶著謙卑和盼望跪在耶穌腳前，承認自己迫切需要赦免。

question.en: What does our view of people living in sin reveal about our hearts? How does Jesus teach us a different way?
question.zh-Hant: 我們如何看待生活在罪中的人，顯示我們有怎樣的心？耶穌如何教導我們以不同的方式待人？

answer.en: The Pharisees were rigid rule followers who looked down on people they considered more sinful than themselves, and Simon was no different. He couldn’t believe Jesus would allow such a sinner to touch Him. This woman was caught up in a darkness she couldn’t defeat on her own, and Simon condemned her for it. But Jesus didn’t; He invited her into His light. So often, we find ourselves sitting in Simon’s seat, judging people who don’t know Jesus for not knowing any better or writing off people who do know Jesus when they stumble. But Jesus’s way—the way of humility and grace—is better.
answer.zh-Hant: 法利賽人嚴格遵守規條，瞧不起他們認為比自己更有罪的人，西門也不例外。他無法相信耶穌會容許這樣的罪人碰祂。這婦人深陷自己無法勝過的黑暗中，西門因此定她的罪。但耶穌沒有；祂邀請她進入祂的光中。我們常常坐在西門的位置上，論斷不認識耶穌的人不懂得正確行事，或在認識耶穌的人跌倒時就放棄他們。但耶穌的道路，就是謙卑和恩典的道路，更為美好。

question.en: Why do the thoughts and motives behind our actions matter? Can we trust Jesus to really see us? Explain.
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼行動背後的思想和動機很重要？我們能相信耶穌真正看見我們嗎？請解釋。

answer.en: Leaders: Share context on hospitality. Luke doesn’t tell us why the woman washed Jesus’s feet with her tears. Maybe she recognized the host’s failure to provide water for Jesus to wash His feet as an insult. Maybe she knew no other way to show her love for Jesus. Whatever her reason for her action, her heart was set on honoring Jesus—and He saw her. Jesus doesn’t want empty worship; He wants humble, repentant hearts set on honoring Him. What we fill our hearts and minds with matters because all of it will spill out in our actions. Others might not notice when we’re faking it, but Jesus will. He knew Simon’s thoughts, after all. Jesus isn’t like anyone else; He sees our hearts clearly. He knows when our love and repentance are real, and to offer Him anything else is empty worship.
answer.zh-Hant: 領袖：分享有關款待的背景。路加沒有告訴我們婦人為甚麼用眼淚洗耶穌的腳。也許她認為主人沒有提供水給耶穌洗腳是侮辱；也許她不知道還能怎樣表達對耶穌的愛。無論她這樣做的原因是甚麼，她的心一意要尊崇耶穌，而祂看見了她。耶穌不要空洞的敬拜；祂要的是謙卑悔改、一心尊崇祂的人。我們讓甚麼充滿心思意念很重要，因為這一切都會流露在行動中。別人可能察覺不到我們的虛假，但耶穌會；畢竟，祂知道西門的想法。耶穌與任何人都不同，祂清楚看見我們的心。祂知道我們的愛和悔改是否真實；向祂獻上其他任何東西，都是空洞的敬拜。

question.en: How did Jesus confront Simon’s thoughts? How does He confront us about our thoughts today?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌如何指出西門的想法？今天祂如何指出我們的想法？

answer.en: Simon was clearly unhappy about the woman coming into his home and making such a grand gesture of love toward Jesus. He probably thought no one would know his feelings about the woman or Jesus. But Jesus doesn’t look at what’s on the outside—He looks at our hearts. Jesus used a story to make His point about what was going on in Simon’s heart—and it wasn’t love or gratitude. For believers today, Jesus speaks through His Word and the Holy Spirit. Both convict us and help us see which of our thoughts honor Jesus and how to “take ... captive” (2 Cor. 10:5) the ones that don’t.
answer.zh-Hant: 西門顯然不喜歡那婦人進入他的家，向耶穌如此隆重地表達愛。他可能以為沒有人會知道他對那婦人或耶穌的感受。但耶穌不看外表，祂看我們的心。耶穌用一個故事指出西門心裏的狀況：那裏沒有愛，也沒有感恩。對今天的信徒來說，耶穌藉著祂的話語和聖靈說話，二者都使我們知罪，幫助我們看見哪些想法尊崇耶穌，也教導我們如何將不尊崇祂的心意「奪回」（哥林多後書 10:5）。

question.en: Why does Jesus deserve our gratitude, regardless of our past or how great or small our sin seems?
question.zh-Hant: 無論我們的過去如何，或我們的罪看似大還是小，為甚麼耶穌都配得我們的感謝？

answer.en: Simon mistakenly assumed that he was set because he was a law-following Pharisee and that only the woman was a “sinner” because she’d been caught in a sinful lifestyle. But both deserved death because their sin made them enemies of God; Jesus offered both life instead (Rom. 6:23). Here’s the thing: No sin is so great that God’s grace can’t cover it, and no sin is so small that it doesn’t need God’s grace. All of us have every reason to be grateful for Jesus’s offer of salvation because even one seemingly tiny sin condemns us to death. Thankfully, no one who accepts Jesus’s gift of salvation is condemned (Rom. 8:1).
answer.zh-Hant: 西門錯誤地以為自己是遵守律法的法利賽人，就已經沒有問題；他認為只有那婦人因為深陷罪惡的生活，才是「罪人」。但他們二人都因罪成為神的仇敵，都該受死；耶穌卻向兩人賜下生命（羅馬書 6:23）。事實是：沒有任何罪大到神的恩典不能遮蓋，也沒有任何罪小到不需要神的恩典。我們每個人都有充分的理由感謝耶穌賜下救恩，因為即使一個看似微小的罪也使我們被定死罪。感謝主，凡接受耶穌救恩禮物的人，都不被定罪（羅馬書 8:1）。

question.en: Why do we need to understand the depth of our sin and how it hurts our relationship with God? How does this understanding make Jesus even better?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼我們需要明白自己的罪有多深，以及罪如何損害我們與神的關係？這樣的認識如何讓我們更看見耶穌的美好？

answer.en: Imagine what the woman in this scenario might have been remembering when she came to Jesus to wash and anoint His feet with perfume. It’s not fun to think about when we’ve messed up—or to look at Jesus’s holy perfection and see our mistakes clearly for what they are: rebellion against a good and loving God. But the more clearly we see our sin, the more we realize our need for a Savior. The more we see that we are powerless to save ourselves, the more we lean into Jesus and see that He is better than anyone or anything else we might trust to save us. So, we can come to Him with confidence, trusting that He has already paid the price for our salvation.
answer.zh-Hant: 想像一下，這婦人來到耶穌面前，用香膏抹祂的腳並為祂洗腳時，可能想起了甚麼。回想自己的過犯並不愉快；看見耶穌聖潔完美，也讓我們清楚看見自己的過錯其實是悖逆良善慈愛的神。但我們越清楚看見自己的罪，就越明白自己需要救主。我們越看見自己無力自救，就越倚靠耶穌，也越看見祂勝過我們可能寄望於拯救自己的任何人或事物。因此，我們可以滿懷信心來到祂面前，相信祂已經付清我們得救的代價。

question.en: When have you seen others as too sinful to be worth your time? What needs to change for you to see them as Jesus does?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在甚麼時候認為別人太有罪，不值得你花時間？要以耶穌的眼光看待他們，你需要改變甚麼？

answer.en: Jesus made people a priority, and He didn’t discriminate because of people’s different cultural or religious beliefs. Jesus went to the people who needed Him. Period. We need to be wise about who we approach—and when and how we approach them—but seeing people as Jesus saw them starts with our hearts. We have to turn our gaze inward to examine ourselves—false beliefs, prejudices, unforgiveness, misunderstandings, and all—before we can ever turn our gaze outward with love and compassion for others. Jesus offers salvation to those we see as “big” sinners just as freely as He offered it to us. When we start with humbly remembering our own need for Him—with remembering the great depths Jesus brought us from—then we remember that we did nothing to deserve salvation. Jesus freely offered it. He paid for our sin with His blood. Like Jesus, we must see those who need Him, approaching them with compassion and leading them to His feet, where they’ll find all the mercy and grace—and ultimately the salvation—they need.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌重視人，沒有因人的文化或宗教信仰不同而歧視他們。耶穌走到需要祂的人當中，就是這麼簡單。我們需要有智慧地決定接近誰，以及何時、如何接近他們，但以耶穌的眼光看人，要從我們的心開始。我們必須先向內省察自己，包括錯誤的信念、偏見、不饒恕和誤解等，才能向外以愛和憐憫看待別人。耶穌白白向我們賜下救恩，也同樣白白地賜給那些我們視為「大」罪人的人。當我們先謙卑地記得自己需要祂，記得耶穌把我們從多深的境地中帶出來，就會記得我們沒有做任何事配得救恩。耶穌白白賜下救恩，祂用自己的血償付我們的罪。我們必須像耶穌一樣，看見需要祂的人，以憐憫接近他們，帶領他們來到祂腳前；他們會在那裏找到所需的一切憐憫和恩典，最終得到救恩。

content.en:
Have you ever taken a personality test? You can find one to suit any personality—from the incredibly detailed Myers-Briggs to the fun quiz you took online to tell you which character you're most like from your favorite book or TV show. While personality tests can help you see yourself in new ways, they don’t actually tell you who you are or what type of person you are. Because the truth is that you are far more than any personality test could imagine or define, no matter how thorough the questions seem.

We often get caught up in personality types, and our brains naturally categorize people as those who are like us and those who aren’t, people who are “good” or “bad,” and even people who are worth our time and people who aren’t. But Jesus isn’t like us. If He looked at us the way we looked at each other, all of us would be doomed. Instead, He sees us with His Father’s eyes, knowing we’re only human but capable of being transformed by the work of the Holy Spirit. This is why Jesus didn’t care “what sort of woman” washed His feet with her tears (Luke 7:39) and why He used a man (Paul, formerly Saul) who once persecuted His people to play a major role in establishing the early church. Maybe you struggle to see how God could love you or forgive you because of what you’ve done in the past, but all that gets washed away with the blood of Jesus (Eph. 2:13). He died for you. Period. No stipulations or fine print can change that. Through Jesus’s life, death, and resurrection, you can be forgiven, free, and made new—no matter who you are, what you’ve done, or how others see you.

Jesus, thank You for looking on me with eyes of love. Give me Your eyes to see others and Your heart to love them well. Help me to see myself as loved, forgiven, and free.
content.zh-Hant:
你曾做過性格測驗嗎？無論是非常詳細的邁爾斯—布里格斯測驗，還是網上有趣的測驗，告訴你最像喜愛的書或電視節目中的哪個角色，總有適合你的性格測驗。性格測驗雖然能幫助你從新角度認識自己，卻不能真正告訴你是誰，或是哪一類人。事實是，無論問題看似多麼周詳，你都遠超過任何性格測驗所能想像或界定的。

我們常常執著於性格類型，大腦也自然地把人分類：與我們相似或不同的人、「好」人或「壞」人，甚至值得或不值得我們花時間的人。但耶穌不像我們。若祂像我們看待彼此那樣看待我們，我們所有人都會滅亡。祂卻以天父的眼光看我們，知道我們不過是人，卻能因聖靈的工作而改變。這就是耶穌不在乎用眼淚洗祂腳的是「怎樣的女人」（路加福音 7:39），也使用一個曾逼迫祂子民的人，就是保羅（從前稱為掃羅），在建立初期教會的事上擔任重要角色的原因。你可能因為過去的所作所為，難以明白神怎能愛你或赦免你，但這一切都被耶穌的血洗淨了（以弗所書 2:13）。祂為你而死，就是如此。沒有任何附帶條件或細則能改變這一點。藉著耶穌的生、死和復活，無論你是誰、做過甚麼，或別人怎樣看你，你都可以蒙赦免、得自由、成為新人。

耶穌，感謝祢用慈愛的眼光看我。求祢賜我祢的眼光看待別人，賜我祢的心好好愛他們。幫助我看見自己是蒙愛、蒙赦免、得自由的人。

question.en: What are you tempted to believe disqualifies you or someone else from becoming a believer or part of your church or small group?
question.zh-Hant: 你容易認為甚麼事會使你或別人沒有資格成為信徒，或加入你的教會或小組？

question.en: When have you wondered how God could love you because of what you’ve done? How does Jesus’s love change your perspective?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾因自己的所作所為而懷疑神怎能愛你嗎？耶穌的愛如何改變你的看法？

prayer.en: Jesus, thank You for looking on me with eyes of love. Give me Your eyes to see others and Your heart to love them well. Help me to see myself as loved, forgiven, and free.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，感謝祢用慈愛的眼光看我。求祢賜我祢的眼光看待別人，賜我祢的心好好愛他們。幫助我看見自己是蒙愛、蒙赦免、得自由的人。

content.en:
We've all had moments when a sinking feeling settled deep in our gut and we wondered, “How am I going to get out of this?” Maybe it was a failing grade, an awkward social situation, an injury or illness that caused you to need help doing everyday tasks. Or maybe you faced a more serious, life-or-death type situation, like being lost in a national park and needing someone to find you. All these scenarios require us to ask others for help—and hope that they respond by coming to our rescue. Some things we just can’t do on our own.

The truth is, no matter the situation you find yourself in now, we all need a Savior. Because of our humanity and our sin, we are completely powerless to save ourselves. Nothing in us and nothing we do could ever make us good enough to stand before God. Only Jesus can do that. Jesus pointed out this truth to Simon, a Pharisee who imagined himself as “all good” before God because his religious community viewed him as righteous. Simon believed only the woman—the “sinner”—needed saving; she did need salvation, but she wasn’t the only one. The woman expressed faith in Jesus by humbly kneeling before Him and grieving her sin, helpless to save herself but recognizing His goodness. And Jesus forgave her.

Jesus doesn’t owe us anything, but He freely gives salvation to those who come before Him with humble repentance and faith—just like the woman in Luke 7. Jesus has done all the work to save us; our only part in our salvation story is to humble ourselves, repent of our sin, and accept the greatest gift we could ever receive.
content.zh-Hant:
我們都曾有過心中一沉、問自己「我要怎樣脫身？」的時刻。也許是成績不及格、尷尬的社交場合，或是受傷生病，需要別人幫忙做日常事務。也許你面對更嚴重、生死攸關的情況，例如在國家公園迷路，需要有人找到你。這些情況都需要我們向別人求助，盼望他們來救援。有些事情我們無法獨自完成。

事實是，無論你現在處於甚麼境況，我們都需要救主。因為我們是人，也因為我們的罪，我們完全無力拯救自己。我們裏面沒有任何東西，我們所做的任何事，也無法使我們足夠良善，可以站在神面前。只有耶穌能做到。耶穌向法利賽人西門指出這個真理；西門因為宗教群體視他為義人，便以為自己在神面前「一切都好」。西門認為只有那婦人，那個「罪人」，需要拯救；她確實需要救恩，卻不是唯一需要的人。婦人謙卑地跪在耶穌面前，為自己的罪哀傷，表達了對祂的信心。她無力自救，卻認識到祂的良善。耶穌赦免了她。

耶穌不欠我們任何東西，卻白白賜救恩給那些像路加福音第 7 章的婦人一樣，以謙卑、悔改和信心來到祂面前的人。耶穌已完成拯救我們的一切工作；我們在得救的故事中所要做的，就是謙卑自己、悔改離罪，接受我們所能得到最寶貴的禮物。

question.en: Which is more difficult for you to accept: that you can’t do anything to save yourself from sin and death or that you must rely on someone else (Jesus) for salvation?
question.zh-Hant: 對你而言，哪一件事更難接受：你無法做任何事拯救自己脫離罪和死亡，還是你必須倚靠另一位，就是耶穌，才能得救？

question.en: How does viewing salvation as a gift affect the way you see Jesus?
question.zh-Hant: 把救恩看作禮物，如何影響你看待耶穌的方式？

prayer.en: LORD JESUS, OPEN MY EYES TO SEE YOU CLEARLY AS MY ONLY SAVIOR AND GIVER OF THE GREATEST GIFT. SHOW ME HOW TO LIVE MY LIFE IN HUMBLE GRATITUDE FOR ALL YOU’VE DONE FOR ME.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，求祢開我的眼睛，清楚看見祢是我唯一的救主，也是賜下最寶貴禮物的主。求祢教導我，為祢所做的一切，以謙卑感恩的心生活。

content.en:
Have you ever been in that awkward situation where someone got you a gift, but you didn’t get anything for them? Maybe you were supposed to show up at a party with a gift but missed the memo. Or maybe someone ahead of you at the coffee shop paid for your order, and you didn’t get to say thank you or didn’t pass it on the person behind you. In these situations, you might’ve felt embarrassed, upset, or even guilty. When people do nice things for us, we want to do nice things for them, or we are inspired to do nice things for others.

Somehow, this doesn’t always translate to our relationship with Jesus. He has given us a gift better than anything we could imagine: salvation from our sin and the hope of eternal life with Him. As believers, we easily become desensitized to this truth because we hear it so often, but that doesn’t make it any less powerful. We might struggle to understand the right response to such a great gift, but that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t respond.

Knowing what Jesus has done for us should change us. When we trust in Jesus for salvation, we receive a completely new identity as children of God (Rom. 8:17; 2 Cor. 5:17)—and children of God live differently, as lights in a dark world. The apostle Paul puts it this way: Our entire lives are to be lived in worship of and in service to the Lord (Rom. 12:1). While Jesus gives tons of instructions for what our new identity should look like and what it means to worship Him with that new identity, He also summed up all God’s commands like this: Love God and love others. This is our right response to all Jesus has done for us.
content.zh-Hant:
你是否曾遇過尷尬的情況：別人送你禮物，你卻沒有為對方預備？也許你本來應該帶禮物參加派對，卻不知道這件事。也許咖啡店裏排在你前面的人替你付了錢，你卻沒有機會道謝，也沒有替後面的人付錢。遇到這些情況，你可能感到尷尬、難過，甚至內疚。當別人善待我們，我們也想善待他們，或受到啟發去善待別人。

不知為何，我們與耶穌的關係卻不一定如此。祂賜給我們一份超乎想像的禮物：從罪中得救，以及與祂同享永生的盼望。作為信徒，我們因為常聽見這真理，很容易變得麻木，但這並不減少它的能力。我們可能不容易明白該如何回應如此重大的禮物，但這不代表我們不應回應。

知道耶穌為我們做了甚麼，應當改變我們。當我們信靠耶穌得救，就得到神兒女的全新身分（羅馬書 8:17；哥林多後書 5:17）；神的兒女活得不一樣，在黑暗的世界中作光。使徒保羅這樣說：我們一生都要敬拜和事奉主（羅馬書 12:1）。耶穌對我們的新身分應如何顯現，以及以這身分敬拜祂是甚麼意思，給了許多教導；祂也把神一切的命令歸納為：愛神、愛人。這就是我們對耶穌為我們所做一切的正確回應。

question.en: How have you responded to the news of Jesus’s great gift to you?
question.zh-Hant: 你如何回應耶穌賜給你這份寶貴禮物的消息？

question.en: What is your response to the idea of living your entire life always for Jesus—to be a living sacrifice? Why?
question.zh-Hant: 想到一生時刻為耶穌而活，作活祭，你有甚麼回應？為甚麼？

prayer.en: JESUS, I CONFESS THAT I OFTEN FORGET JUST HOW GREAT A GIFT MY SALVATION IS. FORGIVE ME FOR THE MOMENTS WHEN I FOCUS ON THE WRONG THINGS, AND GIVE ME THE STRENGTH AND COURAGE TO LIVE OUT MY NEW IDENTITY IN YOU.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，我承認我常常忘記救恩是多麼寶貴的禮物。求祢赦免我專注於錯誤事物的時候，賜我力量和勇氣，活出在祢裏面的新身分。

content.en:
Shame and guilt are not the same, even if we sometimes believe they are because of the way our culture treats people who mess up. Shame means feeling like something you’ve done makes you unworthy of connection, blessing, or love; guilt means recognizing what you did was wrong and accepting the consequences of your actions.

Here’s the thing: All of us, on our own, are unworthy of God’s love and acceptance and belonging to His family. But God loves us because of who He is—because He is love (1 John 4:8). So, He sent Jesus to deal with our shame. Scripture says Jesus went to the cross “despising the shame” of it because of the joy He knew would come through His death (Heb. 12:2). The crucifixion was Jesus’s declaration that shame had no power over Him, and through Him, no power over us either.

Shame over past sin and failure has no place in the life of a believer because that debt has already been paid for and forgiven. But guilt is another story. Guilt, or godly sorrow, comes from conviction, and conviction comes from the Holy Spirit (John 16:8). Conviction isn’t condemnation (telling us we’re doomed because of what we’ve done); conviction is the Holy Spirit revealing our sin to us, feeling grief over it, and turning toward God in repentance. In other words, conviction is a good thing, even when the process hurts! When we mess up, shame tells us to beat ourselves up, but guilt tells us to give up our sins by confessing them to God and trusting Him to forgive us as He has promised (1 John 1:9).
content.zh-Hant:
羞恥和罪疚並不相同，雖然有時受到我們的文化對待犯錯者的方式所影響，我們以為二者一樣。羞恥是覺得自己的所作所為使自己不配與人建立關係、得著祝福或被愛；罪疚則是認識到自己做錯了事，並接受行動的後果。

事實是：單憑自己，我們都不配得到神的愛和接納，也不配屬於祂的家。但神因祂的本性而愛我們，因為祂就是愛（約翰一書 4:8）。因此，祂差遣耶穌來處理我們的羞恥。聖經說，耶穌因知道自己的死將帶來喜樂，就「輕看羞辱」，走上十字架（希伯來書 12:2）。耶穌受釘十字架宣告了羞恥對祂沒有權勢；藉著祂，羞恥對我們也沒有權勢。

過去的罪和失敗帶來的羞恥，在信徒的生命中沒有立足之地，因為那債已經償清，也已蒙赦免。但罪疚則不同。罪疚，或依神心意的憂愁，來自知罪，而知罪是聖靈的工作（約翰福音 16:8）。知罪不是定罪，不是告訴我們因所作所為注定滅亡；知罪是聖靈向我們顯明我們的罪，使我們為罪憂傷，並轉向神悔改。換言之，知罪是好事，即使過程令人痛苦！當我們犯錯，羞恥叫我們苛責自己；罪疚卻叫我們向神認罪，放棄罪惡，並相信祂會按所應許的赦免我們（約翰一書 1:9）。

question.en: Review Luke 7:40. What is the Holy Spirit saying to you right now? What sin could He be calling out?
question.zh-Hant: 重讀路加福音 7:40。聖靈現在對你說甚麼？祂可能正在指出甚麼罪？

question.en: Where do you need to set aside shame over your past and trust that Jesus died to free you from all your sin—past, present, and future?
question.zh-Hant: 面對過去，你在哪方面需要放下羞恥，相信耶穌受死使你脫離過去、現在和將來一切的罪？

prayer.en: God, help me to release any shame I feel over my past and cling to Your grace and to the promise that I am made new. Convict me of sin and help me to accept Your forgiveness.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，求祢幫助我放下對過去的羞恥，緊緊抓住祢的恩典和使我成為新人的應許。求祢指出我的罪，幫助我接受祢的赦免。

content.en:
If you’ve pulled an all-nighter to finish a school project or stayed up way too late hanging out with your family or friends, and then seen something odd, you probably know what it’s like to question your vision. Maybe you blink or rub the sleep from your eyes and try to refocus. Or, if someone is with you, you might even ask, “Did you see that?” We don’t always take in all the details at first glance. Truly seeing what’s in front of us means we must choose to look and set our focus on whatever or whoever it is.

After witnessing Simon’s judgment of the woman who washed His feet with her hair, Jesus turned toward the woman and asked Simon, “Do you see this woman?” (Luke 7:44a). The truth is, Simon didn’t see her; he only saw her sin and her past. And he judged her harshly for it. But Jesus saw the woman. He saw through her sinful past and into her heart, which was humbled before Him in genuine repentance.

Jesus’s eyes constantly settled on those who needed Him, and they were often those others ignored. He teaches us a different way of seeing people, which the apostle Paul describes this way: “We regard no one according to the flesh” (2 Cor. 5:16). When we become new creations in Christ, He gives us new eyes and a fresh perspective to see ourselves and others the way He does. Jesus reminds us that we too were sinners who needed His salvation and are now new creations in Him. With this new heart and new perspective, He helps us see beyond others’ sin and their pasts and into their hearts, which He makes completely new.
content.zh-Hant:
如果你曾為完成學校作業通宵，或與家人朋友相聚到很晚，之後看到奇怪的東西，你可能知道懷疑自己是否看錯是甚麼感覺。也許你眨眨眼或揉去睡意，試著重新看清楚。如果有人和你在一起，你甚至可能問：「你看到了嗎？」我們第一眼不一定能看清所有細節。真正看見眼前的事物，意味著我們必須選擇去看，專注於眼前的人或事。

耶穌看到西門論斷那位用頭髮為祂洗腳的婦人之後，就轉向婦人，問西門：「你看見這女人嗎？」（路加福音 7:44上）事實是，西門沒有看見她；他只看見她的罪和過去，並因此嚴厲地論斷她。但耶穌看見了這婦人。祂看透她罪惡的過去，看見她在祂面前真誠悔改、謙卑的心。

耶穌經常注視著需要祂的人，而這些人往往是別人忽略的。祂教導我們以不同的方式看人，使徒保羅這樣描述：「不憑著外貌認人了」（哥林多後書 5:16）。當我們在基督裏成為新造的人，祂賜我們新的眼光和視角，像祂一樣看待自己和別人。耶穌提醒我們，我們也曾是需要祂拯救的罪人，如今在祂裏面成為新造的人。祂以這顆新心和新視角幫助我們超越別人的罪和過去，看進他們的心，就是祂使之完全更新的心。

question.en: What types of people do you struggle to see with the new eyes Jesus gave you as a believer?
question.zh-Hant: 作為信徒，你難以用耶穌賜給你的新眼光看待哪些人？

question.en: Why is it important to see ourselves rightly in relation to Jesus before we can see others rightly?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼我們要先正確認識自己與耶穌的關係，才能正確看待別人？

prayer.en: Lord Jesus, heal my vision, helping me to see myself rightly and to see others with Your heart and purposes in mind.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，求祢醫治我的眼光，幫助我正確看待自己，並以祢的心意和旨意看待別人。
